candidates.title: Temporary urban art-object as retail-adjacent placemaking
candidates.shift: A moving, temporary 'urban organism' installation (auruBOROS) blurs architecture, public space and collective experience in NYC streets.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: hints at a growing appetite for ephemeral, movable public-experience objects that could migrate into mall/plaza activation strategies — strange because it's non-commercial art functioning as urban infrastructure.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily describes a temporary mobile urban organism connecting architecture, public space and collective experience through NYC.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of art-as-infrastructure blurring lines between installation and public realm; if it spreads, retail/placemaking teams may need new categories for mobile, non-permanent public experience assets rather than fixed storefronts.
candidates.author: Cristina Popescu

candidates.title: Multifunctional infrastructure design reaching remote/underserved farms
candidates.shift: A multidisciplinary infrastructure project designs integrated living/working conditions for isolated community farms to fight poverty and malnutrition.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, off-map (touches SUPPLY CHAIN/INFRASTRUCTURE eventually): if 'intelligent infrastructure' templates for remote community provisioning mature, they could become blueprints for last-mile retail/logistics in underserved geographies.
candidates.evidence: Scientific Reports paper on 'Intelligent Infrastructure Design for Multifunctional Efficient Farm' upgrading isolated-area farm infrastructure and living conditions.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of infrastructure-as-poverty-intervention in peripheral geography; if generalized, could inform how retailers/suppliers design minimal-footprint distribution nodes in low-density, underserved regions.
candidates.author: Nicola Toscani, Matteo Benvenuti, Igor Matteo Carraretto et al.

candidates.title: Designing housing for the 'no standard user' household
candidates.shift: A Madrid apartment renovation explicitly rejects the 'traditional nuclear family' design standard baked into 2000s housing stock, adapting instead to non-standard living arrangements.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a reframing of existing housing stock as demographically obsolete — could foreshadow retail catchment-area assumptions (household size, shopping trip patterns) also needing revision as unit typologies diversify.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily case study: a 78m² Vicálvaro apartment built to 'rigid nuclear family standards' reworked for non-standard living.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of built-form catching up to non-nuclear household demographics; if this spreads, retail-catchment and format planning built on nuclear-family assumptions may need recalibration toward smaller, non-standard households.
candidates.author: Valentina Díaz

candidates.title: Angle-free architecture entering hospitality/retail-adjacent design
candidates.shift: A restaurant design at the Lucas Museum deliberately avoids any 90-degree angles to match biomorphic museum architecture.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, borderline aesthetic trend: pure-curve interiors are costly and non-standard for fit-out trades; if this migrates into flagship retail, it signals rising tolerance for non-modular, non-repeatable construction in experience-led spaces.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen coverage of Rockwell Group's Skywalker Grill interior with no straight 90-degree angles, responding to biomorphic museum architecture.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of flagship experiential design moving away from modular grid construction toward bespoke curved forms; if it spreads to retail flagships, it raises construction cost and skilled-trade requirements for store fit-out.
candidates.author: Dan Howarth

candidates.title: Gender-blind circular procurement undermining CE social goals
candidates.shift: Circular economy procurement policy is being critiqued for ignoring gender equity impacts, meaning circular-material sourcing rules may inadvertently reproduce inequities.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence: no procurement standard yet accounts for gendered labor/ownership effects of circular sourcing — a category gap that construction/materials procurement teams adopting CE mandates may need to fill.
candidates.evidence: Paper in Circular Economy journal analyzing how circular procurement (CP) overlooks gender-equality outcomes in delivering environmental benefits.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a policy/standards absence — circular procurement frameworks lacking equity criteria; if surfaced, construction and retail supply-chain procurement teams adopting circular mandates may face new compliance/reporting categories.
candidates.author: Stephen Kelly, Marzena Reszka, Yiannis Polychronakis

candidates.title: ML-predicted environmental cancer risk as a building/insurance input
candidates.shift: Machine learning models are being developed to predict environmentally-induced cancer risk from chemical, physical and occupational exposures — a data layer that could feed into building/site risk assessment.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, stretched: if such risk models mature, they could become inputs for occupational health insurance underwriting on retail/warehouse sites with known exposure histories — currently no such actuarial product exists.
candidates.evidence: Review paper on ML methods, data and opportunities for predicting environmentally induced cancer risk from air, water, soil and occupational exposures.
candidates.source: World Journal of Innovation and Modern Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of predictive-health data potentially entering site/insurance risk models; if adopted, retail real estate in industrial-adjacent or high-exposure zones could see new insurance products or valuation discounts tied to environmental cancer-risk scores.
candidates.author: Olatunde Adesoji Aladegba

candidates.title: Mining 'bureaucracy debt' to justify deregulation of permitting processes
candidates.shift: New process-intelligence methods quantify accumulated, rarely-reassessed administrative complexity ('bureaucracy debt') to build evidence for deregulation.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence/reframing: no standard metric currently exists for 'regulatory debt' in permitting systems; if adopted by municipalities, it could accelerate or contest zoning/permitting reform timelines for retail construction.
candidates.evidence: Paper proposes process intelligence to mine accumulated administrative complexity (forms, approvals, reporting duties) for evidence-based deregulation.
candidates.source: Annals of Computer Science and Information Systems
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of quantifying regulatory accumulation as an actionable metric; if municipalities adopt 'bureaucracy debt' scoring, permitting and zoning approval timelines for new retail/construction projects could shift materially in either direction.
candidates.author: Wil M. P. van der Aalst

candidates.title: Automated detection of regulatory liability across mass lease/contract portfolios
candidates.shift: NLP tools are emerging to scan tens-of-thousands-strong contract portfolios for regulatory liability exposure faster than legal review capacity can keep up.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: large retailers managing thousands of store leases could adopt this to flag regulatory exposure (zoning, safety, ADA, etc.) automatically — an absence-filler for compliance ops that don't yet scale to portfolio size.
candidates.evidence: Paper describes NLP-driven analytics for detecting regulatory liabilities in enterprise contract portfolios exceeding tens of thousands of active agreements.
candidates.source: Research Journal of Pure Science and Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of compliance automation scaling to portfolio-level lease/contract review; if adopted by big-box or mass retailers, it changes how real-estate/legal teams staff and audit thousands of store leases for regulatory risk.
candidates.author: Uchechi Ngonadi

candidates.title: Computational 'design by availability' for building disassembly
candidates.shift: New computational tools match building design to locally available reclaimed materials to enable design-for-disassembly (DfD), rather than the usual top-down whole-structure planning approach.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: shifts DfD from aspirational guideline to material-availability-driven computation — could become a design-software category retailers' construction/facilities teams use for reuse-first store build-outs.
candidates.evidence: Paper presents a computational approach to facilitate design for disassembly by matching design to material availability, addressing a gap between DfD theory and practice.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of construction design software shifting from prescriptive circularity guidelines to bottom-up, availability-driven design; if adopted, retail construction/facilities teams could source reclaimed materials as a default design constraint rather than an afterthought.
candidates.author: Margherita Lisco

candidates.title: Local, sovereign multimodal LLMs for real-time smart-building analytics
candidates.shift: A local (non-cloud) multimodal LLM architecture is proposed for visual IoT analytics in smart environments, avoiding cloud dependency and rigid rule-based systems.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, directly hits the 'compute?' hunt zone: on-prem AI inference for store sensor/camera data could reshape store-level compute/power requirements and reduce cloud latency/cost dependency for retail CV systems.
candidates.evidence: Paper presents 'Plot-and-Ask', a local multimodal analytics architecture for smart environments processing heterogeneous sensor data in real time without cloud dependency.
candidates.source: Annals of Computer Science and Information Systems
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of edge-AI displacing cloud-dependent smart-building analytics; if adopted in retail, it would change store-level compute/power infrastructure requirements (local GPU/inference hardware) rather than cloud bandwidth, feeding directly into the open 'compute?' question for utilities.
candidates.author: Aygün Varol, Asif Shaikh, Naser Hossein Motlagh et al.

candidates.title: Radon monitoring standards questioned for non-residential building types
candidates.shift: A data-driven review argues that radon monitoring protocols designed for residential buildings are being misapplied to medical (and by extension, other commercial) buildings with different ventilation/occupancy profiles.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence: no radon-monitoring standard yet exists tailored to high-occupancy commercial/retail building types with variable HVAC — a code gap that could extend to big-box retail air-quality standards.
candidates.evidence: Frontiers in Public Health paper reconsiders radon monitoring strategies for Romanian medical buildings, noting current standards don't account for heterogeneous room function/occupancy/HVAC differences from residential settings.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a building-code absence being surfaced: residential-derived monitoring standards misapplied to commercial building types; if extended, retail/warehouse operators may face new indoor-air-quality monitoring obligations distinct from current codes.
candidates.author: Ancuţa Ţenter, Tiberius Dicu, Gabriel Dobrei et al.

candidates.title: Additive manufacturing as circular-economy enabler for plastics
candidates.shift: 3D printing (additive manufacturing) is being positioned as a pathway to circular economy practice in the plastics industry — on-demand production using recycled material with lower input.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, borderline trend: if construction-grade recycled-plastic 3D printing scales, it could reduce material waste in store fixtures/fit-outs and shift materials sourcing toward on-demand, recycled-input manufacturing.
candidates.evidence: Journal of Business Economics case study on advancing circular economy strategies through additive manufacturing in the plastics industry, enabling recycled-material on-demand production.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of manufacturing shifting from virgin-material mass production to on-demand recycled-input additive manufacturing; if scaled to construction components, retail fixtures/fit-out supply chains could source printed recycled-plastic parts rather than injection-molded new plastic.
candidates.author: Alexander Bade, Rebecca Kißner, Jacob Lohmer et al.

candidates.title: Pedestrianization vs. accessibility: disability rights litigation over car-free streets
candidates.shift: Visually impaired residents in Helsinki are taking the city to court, arguing a car-free street is too dangerous to navigate without vehicle-based orientation cues.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a genuine second-order tension nobody has fully resolved — car-free retail-district design (increasingly common) may create new accessibility liabilities requiring redesigned wayfinding/tactile infrastructure, not just fewer cars.
candidates.evidence: Reddit r/urbanplanning post citing legal action: visually impaired advocates suing Helsinki over the car-free Kaivokatu street being judged too dangerous.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of car-free/pedestrianized retail-district design colliding with disability-accessibility law; if litigation succeeds elsewhere, cities and retail landlords may need to retrofit tactile/audio wayfinding into car-free commercial streets, adding cost and design complexity to a widely-praised urban trend.

candidates.title: Waste wool as a novel insulating cladding material for retrofits
candidates.shift: Harvard researchers have developed an insulating cladding tile made from waste wool, positioned specifically for retrofit applications rather than new-build.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: fills a material-absence for retrofit insulation using an agricultural waste stream — could matter for aging big-box retail buildings needing cheap, circular envelope upgrades to meet energy codes.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen reports Harvard's Grinham Research Group presenting 'Upcycling Wool Ecologies' waste-wool insulating cladding tiles at the Oslo Architecture Triennale, shown on a timber-frame retrofit installation.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of agricultural-waste-stream materials entering building envelope retrofit product categories; if commercialized, it offers retail landlords a circular, potentially cheaper insulation upgrade path for aging store stock facing energy-code pressure.
candidates.author: Amy Peacock

candidates.title: Capsule/pod hotel format targeting budget urban travelers at scale
candidates.shift: A backpacker hostel has been converted into a 566-pod capsule hotel with shared social spaces, signaling continued densification of budget hospitality formats in expensive city centers.
candidates.ai_read: Trend: pod/capsule hospitality is already a known format (Japan-originated, spreading to London); included for judgment as it models extreme space-efficiency and shared-amenity design transferable to compact urban retail/experience formats.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen reports SODA's conversion of a London hostel into Otherwander Soho, a 566-pod capsule hotel with vibrant shared social spaces for budget travelers.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of extreme space-density hospitality format maturing in Western gateway cities; already trending, but relevant as a benchmark for how much density/shared-amenity trade-off consumers will accept in physical space, a pattern retail micro-format design could borrow from.
candidates.author: Lizzie Crook

candidates.title: Charred timber facades as mainstream architectural material choice
candidates.shift: Charred-timber cladding (shou sugi ban and variants) continues to appear across a global roundup of buildings, now a recognizable design category rather than a niche technique.
candidates.ai_read: Trend: already a well-covered aesthetic/material trend across residential and hospitality projects globally — included for judgment as a normalized low-maintenance, fire-resistant-adjacent cladding option relevant to store facade material choices.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen roundup of eight buildings globally featuring charred-timber facades, describing it as a recurring technique for dramatic, tactile exteriors.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a niche craft-material technique becoming a mainstream facade choice; probably Context for Kristen, but worth noting as charred-timber's fire-resistance and low-maintenance properties could make it attractive for retail facade retrofits in climate-exposed regions.
candidates.author: Cajsa Carlson
